thread:
incident-bot: PAGER — SEV=P1 — increased 5xx and connection timeouts observed for customers in us-east-1 starting ~1769001200. Detected: route propagation lag and transient BGP flap affecting subnet-us-east-1a. Paging on-call. #oncall

alice: oncall ack, grabbing console and VPC flow logs. seeing spike in 502s from edge->service for a subset of AZa subnets.

ben: I'm coming in too. any change window that might have touched route tables?

carla: infra scheduled a control-plane reboot ~1769000600 for a patch but it was low-risk. tagging infra. I'll DM infra to confirm.

alice: Cloud provider health shows 'route propagation delay' in us-east-1a, and a short-lived BGP flap on the region's peering routers. Routes for rtb-0a1b2c3d (subnet-app-a) missing default route intermittently.

ethan: running quick customer impact query: ~12 tenant environments experiencing increased latency, 3 tenants reporting timeouts for API endpoints. ETA to fix unknown.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-1769001234 — VPC route propagation lag / BGP flap — Assigned: alice (oncall). Severity: P1. Conference bridge: https://call.redwood.example/1769001234

alice: immediate mitigation plan: 1) reroute affected subnets to healthy NAT in us-east-1b via alternative route table 2) force re-association of route tables in 1a 3) if risk, shift traffic to 1b ALB target group 4) inform customers via status page. Doing step 1 now.

alice: CLI I’m running:
```
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0f3e2d1c --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0b9f5a6c
```

alice: route created, but propagation still shows stale state in console for a few minutes. beginning to re-associate subnet with rtb-0f3e2d1c:
```
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id rtb-0f3e2d1c --subnet-id subnet-07aa
```

dino: I'm seeing 502s drop by ~60% after association. network metrics show egress to NAT-0b9f5a6c increased—good sign.

ben: oncall handoff: I’ll monitor for the next 30 mins and prepare rollback steps in case route churn continues. alice, want me to open an SR with provider?

alice: yes please open SR and ask for BGP session diagnostics and any recent peering infra churn. also enabling extra flow log sampling for the affected subnets.

carla: I’ll draft a short status update for status.redwood.ai: "Investigating networking issue in us-east-1 affecting a subset of customers; mitigating by rerouting traffic. No data loss reported. More updates in 30 mins."

ben: SR opened with provider: SR-123456 — asking for BGP adjacency and route-server logs. provider acknowledges and says they're seeing a routing-plane degradation in the AZ.

ethan: quick note on customer impact: two customers on high-throughput pipelines reported partial backpressure; data ingress retried successfully. Will notify CS to proactively reach out to top-tier customers.

alice: observed another small BGP withdraw at 1769002800; propagation delay now ~120s in some cases. still holding on manual associations; don't run automation that flips route tables until we have provider confirmation.

dino: Proactive mitigation: shifting critical ALB target groups to healthy instances in 1b to reduce customer-facing errors. load balancer weight change applied: from 70/30 (1a/1b) to 20/80.

carla: posted status update, pinned in incidents channel and customer status. adding note that some tenants may still see intermittent errors.

incident-bot: Reminder: on-call rotation window near change. Next handoff scheduled at 1769004400.

ben: I'll take over at the handoff. Alice, if you want to sign off earlier that's fine. Otherwise I'll be active at handoff and coordinate with provider.

alice: handing to ben now — summary: mitigations in place (route re-association + temp NAT route + ALB weight shift), traffic reduced errors by ~70%. provider SR pending, they reported control-plane flaps in AZ router cluster. Logging is collected.

ben: taking primary. hitting provider SR for detailed timeline and request for permanent remediation (reboot of affected routing cluster or migrating peering sessions). Also creating follow-up Jira: RED-INC-1769001234.

ethan: capturing customer impact numbers and pushing to postmortem doc. initial assessment: ~15 mins of high error rate, rolling 95th latency doubled for impacted tenants.

carla: ops note — we should add runbook step: if route propagation > 60s, fallback to secondary NAT and re-associate route table programmatically. Filing runbook update in RED-OPS.

ben: provider replied: they performed a targeted restart of peering routers in AZ and cleared BGP flaps at 1769004900. They suggest verifying route table propagation and watching for reappearing withdrawals next 30m.

dino: metrics look stable. errors near baseline, no new withdraws in the past 8 minutes.

ben: closing the immediate customer impact loop — CS notified top 5 customers, status page updated to note resolution in progress. Will keep monitoring until 1769005120 and then transition to follow-up/review.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1769001234 marked 'mitigated' at 1769004999. Postmortem requested.

alice: quick action items: 1) postmortem + timeline 2) add automation checks for route propagation > 60s 3) add alert for repeated BGP withdraws per-AZ 4) verify runbook and test re-association automation in staging. I'll own #1 and #2. Ben please own #4.

ben: will own #4 and coordinate with infra for a more resilient peering failover test.

carla: I’ll schedule customer follow-ups and ensure status page postmortem note goes up once we have RCA.

ethan: logging note — saved VPC flow extracts and packet captures to s3://redwood-incidents/1769001234/ for playbook.

dino: thanks all. leaving monitoring to ben/alice.

ben: final check: if anything spikes ping me. otherwise I'll create the Jira and sketch automation steps.

carla: thanks team — glad we mitigated quickly.
